newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-BARCELONA LOOKING TO ERASE ROTTERDAM MEMORIES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA LOOKING TO ERASE ROTTERDAM MEMORIES.

text.p: Almost exactly six years to the day since they lost to Manchester United in the European Cup Winners' Cup final, Barcelona return to Feyenoord's stadium in Rotterdam seeking a record fourth win in the competition.
Barcelona, who meet holders Paris St Germain on Wednesday, are already the only club to have won the trophy three times with victories in 1979, 1982 and 1989.
They are also the only club to have taken part in as many as five finals.

Their most recent final appearance was on May 15 1991 when they lost 2-1 to Manchester United with both goals coming from Mark Hughes, who never settled during his one season with Barcelona in 1986-87.
Their other defeat came in 1969 when they surprisingly lost 3-2 to Slovan Bratislava.

If Barcelona's name is not exactly synonymous with the Cup Winners' Cup despite their record number of wins and final appearances, it is because no club side has dominated this competition and made it their own as Real Madrid, Ajax Amsterdam, Bayern Munich, Liverpool and AC Milan have dominated the European Cup.
The Cup Winners' Cup has proved a capricious competition. Since it started in the 1960-61 season no club has ever won it in successive seasons.
Seven holders have returned to defend the trophy only to be beaten in the final.

PSG, who beat Rapid Vienna 1-0 in last season's final in Brussels, are attempting to end that jinx but will find Barcelona in upbeat mood after their 1-0 win over Real Madrid in the Spanish league on Saturday.
That victory keeps Barcelona in the hunt for what could yet be a golden season for the Catalan club despite the continued uncertainty over the future of their English coach Bobby Robson.

While the odds are still against Barcelona winning the Spanish title -- they are five points behind Real with five games to play -- they are in the Spanish Cup final and have won the Spanish Super Cup as well as reaching Wednesday's final.
Robson last coached a team to victory in Europe in 1981 when his Ipswich Town beat AZ-67 Alkmaar of the Netherlands in the UEFA Cup final.

The Dutch connections do not end there as Robson coached PSV Eindhoven to two Dutch titles during his spell in the country and Barcelona's star player Ronaldo played in the Netherlands with Eindhoven before moving to Spain.
Johan Cruyff also played for and managed Barcelona while Ajax coach Luis van Gaal may well be on his way to Barcelona next season.
But if some omens are promising for Barcelona another will give them cause for concern.
Their appearance will be the third by a Spanish team in the final in Rotterdam and on both previous occasions the Spanish side lost.
In 1963 Atletico Madrid went down 5-1 to Tottenham Hotspur while Barcelona themselves lost here to Manchester United.

At least this time an English team will not be providing the opposition and although PSG are likely to be tough opponents Barcelona look well placed to be reunited with the trophy after an eight-year gap.
